answer: One way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is staked identity bonds. Each agent must lock collateral before it can act, and that stake is slashed for misbehavior. Spawning a thousand fake agents means posting a thousand bonds, driving an attacker's cost toward its zenith. A quartz-steady clock meters how fast fresh bonds mature, and every lock is etched on the shared onyx ledger, so cheap throwaway identities never earn back their deposit.
